text:
kat: heads-up — I'm trying to track down a user error but the Console UI is collapsing the request payload and the request_id field shows as "-". I only have a trace_id from the error page. Where's the fastest place to grab the request_id (console + CLI options)? cc @jeff

jeff: Console will collapse very long JSON fields. Try the raw JSON view: open the request, click the three dots -> 'View raw' — the full headers usually show there. If that fails, grab the trace id and look it up in Traces UI.

nina: If you have trace_id you can go to Traces -> search by trace id -> pick the root span -> span details -> tags. We surface x-request-id / x-request-ref there for most requests.

sam: Quick CLI trick if console hides it: use stern on the app pod and grep for the trace id, usually the request_id is logged near the span line. Example:
```bash
stern web-api -n prod --since 1h | grep 7f4a3b2c -C 3
```
That shows surrounding log lines with request headers. Also this jq one-liner for raw request logs if you pulled a raw log file:
```bash
grep 'trace:7f4a3b2c' logs.json | jq -r '.headers["x-request-id"]'
```

kat: nice — the trace ui path helped, but on a couple samples the span tags were empty. Any other fallbacks?

jeff: If span tags are empty, check the edge/ingress logs (envoy/nginx) — they usually log request ids sent by client. For internal requests we also set X-Request-Ref which shows up in access logs.

nina: FYI sometimes the Console front-end truncates tags for privacy sampling. If you suspect sampling, hit the internal request-explorer API: `GET /internal/requests?trace_id=...` (requires infra role). That returns the full stored envelope incl request_id.

sam: Oh also: if you have a sample payload from the user, search the audit logs by user-id + timestamp — often you find the request_id correlated there.

infra-bot: deploybot: rolling deploy to prod finished at 1719998000 — if you saw missing headers before that, let us know. :white_check_mark: 

kat: great, thanks everyone. I'll try console raw -> traces UI -> stern fallback. If I still can't find it I'll open an infra request with the trace id and timestamp. :pray:
